title: Bridging Relativistic Twisted Fermion Beams and Photonic OAM Flux in Gauged Hopf Lattices: Emergent Topological Analogs
abstract: Recent work has demonstrated non-diffractive topological spin textures (Skyrmion- and meron-like) that persist in the core of diffracting relativistic twisted fermion beams [1]. Here we present numerical simulations of an analogous photonic system: Laguerre-Gaussian (LG) twisted photon packets coupled to a gauged Hopf lattice with discrete flux flywheels. Our results reveal emergent behavior of the same qualitative class, including persistent core features under propagation, mean survival approx 0.150 at critical lambdat = 2 clustering tightly with the mystery scale e^{-2} approx 0.1353 and residual R approx 0.1375, golden-angle correlations in the OAM mode ladder, and topological residuals with long-lived structure. Multi-l simulations further exhibit z-resolved flux transfer and twist dynamics that play a role analogous to probability-current continuity in the fermionic setting. These findings suggest photonic platforms as accessible analogs for exploring topological textures in structured waves, and they formalize a concrete computational bridge between relativistic twisted matter waves and topological photonics.
summary: This paper develops a computational bridge by simulating the behavior of twisted photons coupled into a gauged Hopf lattice. The study finds that these photonic systems exhibit emergent topological features, such as persistent core structures and specific quantized correlations, mirroring non-diffractive textures observed in relativistic fermion beams. This suggests photonics is an accessible analog platform for exploring universal concepts in topological matter waves.
main_problem: The primary goal is to establish a computational bridge by finding analogous topological phenomena between relativistic twisted fermion beams and photonic systems.
main_result: The simulations show that coupling OAM flux into a gauged Hopf lattice results in emergent core features, persistent survival rates near specific constants ($e^{-2}$), and golden-angle correlations mirroring fermionic findings.
method: Numerical simulations are employed to model the evolution of Laguerre-Gaussian (LG) twisted photon packets coupled to a gauged Hopf lattice using relaxation PDEs.
model_or_system: The system involves two parts: 1) A reference fermionic model exhibiting non-diffractive topological spin textures, and 2) The photonic analog, which uses LG OAM packets propagating through a lattice governed by a PDE incorporating gauge damping torque.
key_observables: Mean survival of twist ($\approx 0.150$), Topological Residual ($R \approx 0.1375$), Golden-Angle Correlations in the OAM ladder, and z-resolved flux transfer.
important_parameters: Critical normalization $\lambda_t = 2$, Gauge damping parameter $\kappa$, and the characteristic constants $e^{-2} \approx 0.1353$ and $R$.
main_assumptions: The analogy is based on shared geometric/continuity constraints rather than a direct microscopic duality; the lattice PDE is calibrated, not derived from first principles.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the conceptual bridge between fermion cores and OAM flux transfer into the Hopf lattice. Figure 2 shows mean survival vs. gauge damping ($\kappa$), and Figure 4 displays golden-angle packing and the pump–relax trajectory near $\{R, e^{-2}\}$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the fermionic context, then details the photonic model (LG packets on Hopf lattice), presents simulations showing emergent topological signatures (survival plateau, flux transfer), and concludes by formalizing the computational bridge between the two domains.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it uses quantum optics (OAM/photonic lattices) to model complex many-body physics concepts (topological protection in fermions), offering a concrete platform for testing universal physical principles.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Conceptual bridge between regimes. Left: non- diffractive τTL core (antiparallel configuration) for a relativis- tic twisted fermion beam, with overall diffraction of the inten- sity envelope. Center: OAM flux transfer from an LG twisted photon packet. Bottom: deposition into a gauged Hopf lattice of flux flywheels, with labels highlighting e−2 survival at crit- ical λt = 2 (mystery convention), golden-angle correlations, and topological residuals. This figure frames the fermionic ↔ photonic analogy developed in the present work. (Simulation stack: oam flux v0.5-preprint.)

FIG. 2. Data-true emergent survival sweep from frozen oam flux emergence probes (report.json; ℓ= 3, λt = 2). (a) Mean survival after pump–relax versus gauge damping κ ∈[0.80, 0.90]. Horizontal lines: residual R ≈0.1375, mystery scale e−2 ≈ 0.1353, and golden-angle fraction. Vertical markers: κdoc = 0.85, κ⋆≈0.851, κsim ≈0.89. Measured mean survival ≈0.150 (∼11% above e−2, ∼9% above R). (b) Holonomy gap B(κ) = π2(e/π −κ) crosses zero at κ⋆and meets R near κdoc.

FIG. 3. Data-true multi-ℓz-resolved flux transfer from live VQC coupling (oam flux; kkick = 0.008 so the photon reservoir drains over many z steps rather than in a single kick). (a) Instantaneous ledger deposit |∆pledger| (log1p-normalized): transfer scales with |ℓ| (dark band at ℓ= 0 where OAM momentum vanishes) and extinguishes earlier for low-|ℓ| modes as p0 is exhausted. (b) Cumulative fraction of initial OAM momentum p0 transferred to the lattice; mid-|ℓ| channels approach ∼50% transfer by z = 5 in this kick window.

FIG. 4. Data-true golden-angle and residual diagnostics (κ = 0.85, ℓ= 3). Left: Vogel golden-angle packing in the transverse plane with the dynamical core at the origin; spokes mark golden-quantized OAM modes ℓ∈{−5, −4, 5} selected by the emergence probe (phase increments closest to multiples of ≈137.5◦). Right: instrumented pump–relax trajectory versus normalized λt. Mean survival S (blue) and residual feature S −R (green) plateau through the pump half-interval, then decay in pure PDE relaxation toward the {R, e−2} band (horizontal references). The red dashed line marks the pump→relax switch at τ = 1.
